beats.text: An Ikoyi rooftop, but not the rooftop. A private room behind it, booked out. Oud smoke, a brass teapot, one table. The staff only come when he rings.
No photos tonight. Not because of you. Because of everyone else.
{tell}

arranged.text: His phone buzzes once. 'My mother,' he says. 'She says I must be serious this year.' He says it to the teapot, not to you.

kano_wife.text: When he leans over to pour your tea, a gold ring on a thin chain swings out of his kaftan collar. He tucks it back like a reflex.

defiant_love.text: A waiter whispers to him. He stands: 'We leave through the kitchen. Trust me.' The cooks don't even look up. They've seen this before.

choices.label: Phones away. Tea, oud and his full attention.
choices.receipt: You put your phone away and kept him a secret.

outcomes.text: He talks like a man who has rationed words for years. At midnight his aide hands you an envelope: 'For your fuel.' You don't drive.

defiant_love.text: Three hours. His father's rigs, his mother's laugh. 'I've never said this much to anyone.' The envelope says 'For your fuel.' You don't drive.

choices.label: Post the teapot. Just the teapot. Nobody will know.
choices.receipt: You posted the teapot from his private room.

outcomes.text: Just a teapot. 900 views and one question: 'Who's the Alhaji?' You say nothing. Power.
His reflection is in the brass. Cream cap, bespoke cuff. Zoom culture is undefeated.

choices.label: "Why the secrecy, Bello? Be honest."
choices.receipt: You asked him why you had to be a secret.

outcomes.text: 'In my family, everything is somebody's business. I wanted one thing that was only mine.' Lovely. Not an answer.

arranged.text: 'My family has plans for me. I haven't agreed to them.' Haven't. Yet.

kano_wife.text: 'Lagos talks. Kano listens.' He refills your tea instead of finishing the sentence.

defiant_love.text: 'Because my family will try to buy you or scare you. I wanted you to meet me before you meet them.' He means it.

'Then this is a transaction.' He pays the bill, and the warmth leaves with the waiter.

kano_wife.text: 'The Lagos subsidiary. The Kano one is... family-run.' Family-run.

beats.text: A members' lounge on Ozumba Mbadiwe with no sign on the door. Bello has laid out twelve tiny bottles of oil on black velvet.
Everyone I care about has their own scent. So I can find them in a dark room. Let me make yours.
{tell}

kano_wife.text: 'Lagos gossip. Ignore.' Then he books an extra flight to Kano. Damage control has a timetable.

defiant_love.text: 'My uncle leaked it. He wants you scared off. Are you scared?' Then: 'I'm not.'

choices.label: "This smells like Alhaji Sani."
choices.receipt: You named his uncle as the source.

outcomes.text: He goes silent for a minute. 'How do you know that name?' 'You told me.' 'I did.' He sounds proud.

arranged.text: 'Alhaji Sani arranges everything,' he says. 'Including me.'

kano_wife.text: 'My uncle? No. My uncle has... other concerns. In Kano.'

choices.label: Text him one word: 'Tea.'
choices.receipt: You sent him the one word he gave you.

outcomes.text: 'Not tonight. I'm sorry.' The word worked. He just didn't.

defiant_love.text: He's at your gate in forty minutes. No aide, no driver. 'Nobody scares you out of my life. Not even a blog.'

beats.text: His flat, Saturday. The door opens and a young woman walks in with a tape measure and her mother.
Sorry. They said measure the curtains for after the wedding. I'm Amina. Nobody told me your name.
{tell}

arranged.text: On the counter, a fresh box of cream wedding cards. 'Bello weds Amina. March 14th.' Gold Arabic calligraphy.

choices.label: Make her tea. Ask her what she wants.
choices.receipt: You made his fiancée tea and listened.

outcomes.text: She's twenty-four, a pharmacist in Kaduna, and she didn't choose this either. 'He's kind,' she says. 'He's just not brave.'

choices.label: "Bello. Choose. Right now."
choices.receipt: You made him choose in front of her.

outcomes.text: 'You,' he says. Then his phone rings: 'Mama'. He answers it.
He looks at you, at her mother, then at the floor. The floor wins.

choices.label: "Congratulations to you both." Leave the key.
choices.receipt: You congratulated them and left his key behind.

outcomes.text: You put the key beside the wedding cards. Amina says 'sorry' as you go. She means it more than he does.

choices.label: Go live from his balcony. Narrate everything.
choices.receipt: You livestreamed his fiancée's visit.

outcomes.text: #BelloAndAmina was supposed to trend in March. It trends today, with you narrating.

choices.label: "I'll still be here after March."
choices.receipt: You promised to stay after his wedding.

outcomes.text: Amina looks at you with pity. He looks at you with relief. One look is worse. He presses ₦300k into your hand: 'For your patience.'

choices.label: "I kept your secret from day one. Price?"
choices.receipt: You named your price for staying invisible.

outcomes.text: ₦900k lands before her mother finds the curtain rail. Silence has a wedding budget too.

choices.label: "Day one. Your boot. 'My cousin's.'"
choices.receipt: You reminded him of the cards in his boot.

outcomes.text: He can't look at you. Amina can. 'He told me you were his cousin too.'

choices.label: "I saw you both in that lobby."
choices.receipt: You told her you'd seen her in the lobby.

outcomes.text: Amina nods. 'Awolowo Road. You walked past us. I knew then.' Of course she did.

choices.label: "Does she smell like me too?"
choices.receipt: You asked if he'd made her a scent too.

outcomes.text: Amina sniffs the air. 'He bought mine. Yours he made.' She leaves the tape measure on the floor and walks out first.

choices.label: Show Amina the photo he made you delete.
choices.receipt: You showed his fiancée the deleted photo.

outcomes.text: She studies it. 'He's never laughed like that with me.' She sends it to her mother. Then to his.

choices.label: "So the flat in my cousin's name was for after March."
choices.receipt: You asked if your flat was his after-March plan.

outcomes.text: He doesn't deny it. 'I wanted you somewhere safe. Somewhere I could still come.' Amina writes the address down.

beats.text: Sunday morning. You surprise him at his flat with akara and pap. Someone else has already made breakfast.
Ina kwana. I'm Hauwa. His wife. You must be the Lagos one.
{tell}

kano_wife.text: On her finger: the twin of the ring he wears on a chain under his kaftan.

choices.label: Sit down. Eat. Let her talk.
choices.receipt: You sat down and let his wife talk.

outcomes.text: An hour, calmly. Kano, eight years, two children. 'You are not the first Lagos one,' she says. 'You are the first he hid this well.'

choices.label: Wake him up. Make him explain. Now.
choices.receipt: You woke him up to explain himself.

outcomes.text: He comes out in a singlet, sees you both, and sits down on the floor like a man in a film. 'I was going to tell you.' Both of you laugh. Not kindly.

choices.label: Put the breakfast down. Leave. Block him in the lift.
choices.receipt: You left breakfast for his wife and blocked him.

outcomes.text: Hauwa calls after you: 'Take your akara! You paid for it!' Kano manners. You block him between floors.

choices.label: Photograph her. Post: "Meet the wife."
choices.receipt: You posted his wife on the Parlour.

outcomes.text: The Parlour goes feral. Her brother comments within the hour. Kano and Lagos, united at last, against him.

choices.label: "I don't mind sharing."
choices.receipt: You told his wife you didn't mind sharing.

outcomes.text: Hauwa raises one eyebrow. 'He minds. Very much.' That afternoon he sends ₦250k: 'For Sunday.'

choices.label: "Invisible was your rule. Invisible has a price."
choices.receipt: You named your price for staying invisible.

outcomes.text: ₦1m lands before Hauwa finishes her kunu. 'Please,' he texts. Just that.

choices.label: "Every other Friday. 6:40 to Kano. I counted."
choices.receipt: You told her you'd counted his Kano flights.

outcomes.text: Hauwa laughs. 'He told you the flight number? He doesn't even tell me the flight number.'

choices.label: "Your sister already met me. At a salon."
choices.receipt: You told her you'd met her sister.

outcomes.text: Hauwa nods. 'Rabi told me. Saffron and rose. I came to see for myself.' She looks at him. 'He's getting lazy.'

choices.label: Show her the photo from the birthday dump.
choices.receipt: You showed his wife the photo he made you delete.

outcomes.text: She looks for a long time. 'He told me he was in Abuja that night.' Now two of you know where he was.

choices.label: "Is that why your school fees came through me?"
choices.receipt: You asked whose money went through your account.

outcomes.text: Hauwa frowns. 'The fees came from a Lagos account this term.' She looks at you. 'Yours?' She is not angry at you. That's worse.

choices.label: "I saw your brother in that restaurant lobby."
choices.receipt: You told her you'd seen her brother looking for him.

outcomes.text: 'Idris? He was looking for this one.' She points at her husband with a spoon. 'He said Bello ran through a kitchen.'

choices.label: "Is my cousin's-name flat because of you?"
choices.receipt: You asked his wife about the flat he gave you.

outcomes.text: 'A flat?' Hauwa turns to him slowly. 'You told me Lagos was expensive.' You both watch him find a new interest in the ceiling.

beats.text: A private lounge on Ozumba Mbadiwe. Bello's uncle is waiting alone, with tea and a leather briefcase. He doesn't stand.
My nephew will marry who his family chooses. Here is one million naira. There are four more if you are gone by Friday.
{tell}

defiant_love.text: A phone buzzes on the table: 'Bello'. Nine missed calls. The uncle silences it without looking.

choices.label: Push the briefcase back. Call Bello.
choices.receipt: You refused his uncle's money and called him.

outcomes.text: He arrives in eleven minutes, out of breath, cap crooked. He takes your hand in front of his uncle. 'Uncle. Meet the person I'm choosing.'

choices.label: Take the money. A million is a million.
choices.receipt: You took his uncle's money.

outcomes.text: You take it. Bello knows by midnight. He doesn't shout. 'He told me everyone has a price. I said not you.'

choices.label: Record him secretly. Send it to the Parlour.
choices.receipt: You leaked his uncle's bribe to the Parlour.

outcomes.text: 'Oil family tries to buy off Lagos lover' trends by morning. His family is humiliated. So, quietly, is Bello.

choices.label: "Why are you so afraid of me, Alhaji?"
choices.receipt: You asked his uncle why he was afraid of you.

outcomes.text: He sips his tea. 'He has never disobeyed me. Because of you, he has done it eleven times this month.' He almost smiles.

choices.label: [Runs] "Make it ten, and I'll think about it."
choices.receipt: You haggled with his uncle.

outcomes.text: He pays two, smiling. You text Bello everything from the lift. He laughs: 'Keep it. It's my inheritance anyway.'
Bello walks in on the words 'make it ten'. He leaves without a sound.

choices.label: "He made me a scent. He doesn't do that for 'temporary'."
choices.receipt: You told his uncle about the scent.

outcomes.text: The uncle leans in, sniffs once, sits back. 'Saffron and rose. His grandmother's.' He closes the briefcase. 'So it's like that.'

choices.label: "You're the Alhaji Sani he warned me about."
choices.receipt: You told his uncle you'd been warned about him.

outcomes.text: 'He warned you?' A pause. 'Good. Then he's serious.' The uncle pours your tea himself.

choices.label: Call Aisha. Put her on speaker.
choices.receipt: You put his sister on speaker with his uncle.

outcomes.text: Aisha: 'Uncle, if you send them away, I'm not coming to my own wedding.' He puts his cup down very carefully.

choices.label: "He's telling the family in March. Wait for March."
choices.receipt: You told his uncle to wait for March.

outcomes.text: The uncle studies you. 'He told you March? He told me never.' He leaves the briefcase and the bill.

choices.label: "You were in that lobby, looking for my face."
choices.receipt: You told his uncle you'd seen him hunting for you.

outcomes.text: 'And you walked out the front door to show me.' He nods slowly. 'Brave. My nephew needs brave.'

choices.label: Show him the key tag: 'Ours, when they let us.'
choices.receipt: You showed his uncle the key Bello gave you.

outcomes.text: He reads the label twice. 'His handwriting has not changed since he was nine.' He hands it back gently.

beats.text: Admiralty Way salon. The woman in the next chair leans over and sniffs, very politely.
Sorry. That oud. Saffron, rose, a little smoke. Only one man in Lagos blends that. Bello?

choices.label: "It's from a shop in Balogun."
choices.receipt: You denied the scent was his.

outcomes.text: She smiles like she's heard that before. 'Of course.'

arranged.text: 'Of course.' She photographs her nails, and you. 'My cousin Amina will love this colour.' Amina.

kano_wife.text: 'Of course. My sister Hauwa has the same one. From the same shop.' She doesn't blink.

defiant_love.text: 'Of course,' she says, delighted. 'I'm Aisha. His sister. He's never made one for anyone but our mother.'

choices.label: "Yes. He made it for me."
choices.receipt: You admitted Bello made you the scent.

outcomes.text: She nods slowly and says nothing else.

arranged.text: Her smile drops. 'He made you one? He bought one for Amina. Bought.' She leaves without her change.

kano_wife.text: 'He made one for you. Eight years, my sister got hers from duty free.' She leaves with her nails half-done.

defiant_love.text: 'Then it's serious.' She hugs you, wet nails and all. 'I'm Aisha. His sister. I've been waiting for you.'

choices.label: "How do you know his blend?"
choices.receipt: You asked how she knew his blend.

outcomes.text: 'Everyone in his family knows it.'

arranged.text: 'Everyone at the engagement smelled it.' Engagement. She says it like weather.

kano_wife.text: 'My sister wears the other one. In Kano.' She shows you a wedding photo. It's him.

defiant_love.text: 'Because I'm his sister, and I've smelled that blend once before. On our mother.'

beats.text: A DM from an account with no picture.
Saw your post. I know that cuff. I know that teapot. Who are you to him?

choices.label: Block. Delete. Pretend it's spam.
choices.receipt: You blocked the stranger who knew him.

outcomes.text: Blocked. Your hands are still shaking a little.

choices.label: "Who's asking?"
choices.receipt: You asked the stranger who they were.

outcomes.text: No reply. Just 'seen'.

arranged.text: 'Amina's cousin. The bride.' Bride.

kano_wife.text: 'I sewed that cuff. In Kano. For my husband.' Then she blocks you.

defiant_love.text: 'His uncle's office. Alhaji would like a meeting.' A meeting. Like a contract.

choices.label: Forward it to Bello.
choices.receipt: You forwarded the DM to Bello.

outcomes.text: 'Delete your post. Please.' Then: 'I'll handle it.'

arranged.text: 'Delete it. Now.' Then nothing for six hours.

kano_wife.text: 'Who sent this? Send me the account.' He doesn't ask if you're okay.

defiant_love.text: 'That's my uncle's office. I'm coming over.' He arrives with tea and a plan.

beats.text: You posted us. I asked for one thing. Invisible. Why?

choices.label: "I'm sorry. I wanted one person to know."
choices.receipt: You apologised for posting him.

outcomes.text: He sits with that a long time. 'I know,' he says. 'I want that too.'

defiant_love.text: 'One person,' he repeats. 'Soon it'll be everyone. I promise.'

choices.label: "Why can't anyone know, Bello? Say it."
choices.receipt: You demanded to know why you had to be hidden.

outcomes.text: He opens his mouth. Closes it. 'Not tonight.'

arranged.text: 'Because in March I'm expected somewhere. And I'm a coward about it.' Honest, finally.

kano_wife.text: 'Because some people in Kano read Lagos statuses.' He picks his words like a man crossing a river on stones.

defiant_love.text: 'Because my uncle will come for you, and I'm not ready to lose. Give me until March.'

choices.label: "I'll post you again. Proudly."
choices.receipt: You told him you'd post him again.

outcomes.text: He stands. 'Then post an empty chair.' He leaves his tea untouched.

beats.text: Good morning. ₦30 million passed through your account this week. We need the source of funds by Friday, or we escalate.

choices.label: Call Bello: "Your money, your explanation."
choices.receipt: You made Bello explain the money to your bank.

outcomes.text: He sends a letter on company letterhead. The officer says 'okay' in a voice that isn't okay.

arranged.text: His letter, on family letterhead: 'Bride price disbursement.' The officer reads it aloud, slowly.

kano_wife.text: His letter: 'Family support, Kano household.' Household.

defiant_love.text: He's at the bank in an hour with lawyers and statements. 'It's mine. They were helping me.' The officer apologises to you.

choices.label: Pay a lawyer to answer for you.
choices.receipt: You paid a lawyer to deal with the bank.

outcomes.text: Three paragraphs later the bank closes the file. Your lawyer opens an invoice.

choices.label: Ignore it. Banks forget.
choices.receipt: You ignored the bank's compliance call.

outcomes.text: Banks do not forget. Your card is declined at a petrol station in Ikeja. In front of a queue.

beats.text: About the trip. March 14th. I... can we talk about the dates?

choices.label: "No. March 14th. Pack light."
choices.receipt: You refused to move your March trip.

outcomes.text: Silence. Then: 'Okay.' It doesn't sound okay.

arranged.text: 'I can't do the 14th.' ₦500k arrives: 'Change the dates. Please. I'll explain.' He won't.

kano_wife.text: 'I can't do March. Family in Kano.' He sends money for a solo trip. Generous. Absent.

defiant_love.text: A long pause. 'Okay. I'll tell my family on the 13th, then. Pack light for both of us.'

choices.label: "Fine. You pick the dates."
choices.receipt: You let him move your March trip.

outcomes.text: He picks April. 'After things settle.' Things.

defiant_love.text: He picks March 15th. 'One day to tell them. The rest of my life to tell you.' Cheesy. Devastating.

choices.label: "What happens on March 14th, Bello?"
choices.receipt: You asked him what happens on March 14th.

outcomes.text: 'Nothing you need to worry about.' Which is exactly what people say about things you need to worry about.

arranged.text: A long silence. 'A wedding,' he says. 'Not ours.'

kano_wife.text: 'An anniversary. A business one.' A business anniversary.

defiant_love.text: 'Nothing yet. That's the point. I want it to be the day I tell them about you.'

beats.text: Long day. My mother says I must be serious this year. Anyway. Plan anything you want for us. Just know I'll be in Kaduna most of March.

choices.label: "Noted. March is Kaduna. I'll miss you."
choices.receipt: You caught that March is Kaduna.

outcomes.text: 'You listen,' he replies. Then: 'Few people do.'

choices.label: "Serious about what, exactly? 👀"
choices.receipt: You asked what 'serious' meant.

outcomes.text: A laughing emoji, then nothing. A man dodging a question in emoji.

choices.label: "Kaduna? Bring me kilishi."
choices.receipt: You asked him for kilishi.

outcomes.text: His driver drops three kilos of kilishi at your gate. No note. Love language: dried meat.

beats.text: Sorry I missed your call. My uncle again. He runs the family like a board meeting with no minutes. If an Alhaji Sani ever calls you, don't pick.

choices.label: "Alhaji Sani. Blocked in advance."
choices.receipt: You caught his uncle's name.

outcomes.text: 'Good.' A pause. 'He's not a bad man. He just thinks he owns the weather.'

choices.label: "Why would your uncle call me?"
choices.receipt: You asked why his uncle would call you.

outcomes.text: 'He wouldn't. Probably.' Probably.

choices.label: "Board meeting? Send me minutes and money."
choices.receipt: You asked him for minutes and money.

outcomes.text: ₦30k. 'Minutes to follow.' They never do.

beats.text: Can't do this Friday. Or the one after next. Every other Friday I take the 6:40 to Kano. Business, family, you know how it is.

choices.label: "6:40 to Kano, every other Friday. Noted."
choices.receipt: You caught his Kano Fridays.

outcomes.text: 'You're very precise,' he says. You are.

choices.label: "Bring me back a kaftan."
choices.receipt: You asked for a kaftan from Kano.

outcomes.text: He brings two. Hand-embroidered. Your tailor weeps.

choices.label: "Which family, Bello?"
choices.receipt: You asked him which family.

outcomes.text: A voice note of him laughing. Only laughing.

beats.text: Good morning. My sister Aisha is the only one in my family who knows about you. If she ever calls, she's safe. She's the only one who is.

choices.label: "Aisha is safe. Saving her number."
choices.receipt: You caught that Aisha is safe.

outcomes.text: 'She'll like you,' he says. 'She likes trouble.'

choices.label: "Only one? Why only one?"
choices.receipt: You asked why only his sister knows.

outcomes.text: 'Because the others would have opinions.' Opinions is doing a lot of work.

choices.label: "Tell Aisha I need her stylist."
choices.receipt: You asked for his sister's stylist.

outcomes.text: A stranger's voice note: 'Who is this?' Then a stylist's number. Family bonding.

beats.text: Twelve courses tonight and nothing tastes like home. My mother's tuwo shinkafa and miyan kuka. Nobody in Lagos gets it right.

choices.label: "Tuwo shinkafa and miyan kuka. Challenge accepted."
choices.receipt: You caught his favourite meal.

outcomes.text: 'Don't threaten me with a good time.'

choices.label: "Twelve courses?? Pack some for me."
choices.receipt: You asked him to pack you leftovers.

outcomes.text: His aide drops four takeaway boxes at your gate. Tiny portions. Enormous plates.

choices.label: Send a photo of your noodles.
choices.receipt: You sent him your noodles.

outcomes.text: 'Is this what you eat?' ₦20k arrives: 'Food. Real food.'

beats.text: Lagos is loud. If you ever need me, don't call. Calls get seen. Send one word: 'Tea.' I'll find a way.

choices.label: "One word. Tea. Got it."
choices.receipt: You caught his one-word signal.

outcomes.text: 'Good,' he says. 'I've never given anyone that word.'

choices.label: "Why can't I just call like a normal person?"
choices.receipt: You asked why you can't just call.

outcomes.text: 'Because nothing about this is normal yet.' Yet.

choices.label: "Tea? I prefer zobo."
choices.receipt: You told him you prefer zobo.

outcomes.text: A crate of zobo arrives with a note: 'Fine. Zobo.' Romance, Hausa edition.
